recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-19427 unless PA later decides to standardize a DICOM payload type value or change the Endpoint payload advertising model.
issue_request: FHIR-19427 asked for a suitable Endpoint payloadType code for DICOM/DICOMweb payloads or for payloadType to stop being mandatory; Jira is Published/Persuasive with Modification and resolves the issue by citing FHIR-25393, which changed payloadType to 0..*.
initial_application: No standalone FHIR-19427 source commit was found. Commit 445d4741d1559c197decca8343f60d1cad753d36 changed Endpoint.payloadType min from 1 to 0, and merge commit 29c32a3f611f298e0601cd090b441155fed47286 for PR #1832 explicitly listed FHIR-19427 among the Endpoint cardinality trackers.
additional_context: Endpoint is active in source/fhir.ini, and the former Endpoint.payloadType element now maps to Endpoint.payload.type. The originating Zulip thread and PA WGM minutes support the interpretation that mandatory payloadType plus an example binding caused the DICOM problem; PA approved relaxing the element rather than requiring a new DICOM payload code. Related audits for FHIR-22629, FHIR-25393, FHIR-34261, and FHIR-39617 were already on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative Endpoint StructureDefinition defines Endpoint.payload.type with min 0 and max *, so DICOM endpoints are no longer forced to provide an unsuitable payload type code.
